entries.reader_content_plain:
CHAPTER 26

 2Ch 26:1-8 . Uzziah Succeeds Amaziah and Reigns Well in the Days of Zechariah.

 1. Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah-- (See on 2Ki 14:21 ; 2Ki 15:1 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4104"/><div sID="gen5947" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4104"/><hi type="bold">2. He built Eloth--</hi>or, "He it was who built Eloth." The account of the fortifications of this port on the Red Sea, which Uzziah restored to the kingdom of Judah (<reference osisRef="2Chr.33.13">2Ch 33:13</reference>), is placed before the chronological notices (<reference osisRef="2Chr.26.3">2Ch 26:3</reference>), either on account of the importance attached to the conquest of Eloth, or from the desire of the historian to introduce Uzziah as the king, who was known as the conqueror of Eloth. Besides, it indicates that the conquest occurred in the early part of his reign, that it was important as a port, and that Hebrew merchants maintained the old trade between it and the countries of the East [Bertheau]. <div eID="gen5947" type="x-p"/>

 2Ch 26:9 , 10 . His Buildings.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4109"/><div sID="gen5954" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4109"/><hi type="bold">9. Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem, &c.--</hi>whence resistance could be made, or missiles discharged against assailants. The sites of the principal of these towers were: at the corner gate (<reference osisRef="2Chr.25.23">2Ch 25:23</reference>), the northwest corner of the city; at the valley gate on the west, where the Joppa gate now is; at the "turning"--a curve in the city wall on the eastern side of Zion. The town, at this point, commanded the horse gate which defended Zion and the temple hill on the southeast [Bertheau]. <div eID="gen5954" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4110"/><div sID="gen5955" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4110"/><hi type="bold">10. Also he built towers in the desert--</hi>for the threefold purpose of defense, of observation, and of shelter to his cattle. He dug also a great many wells, for he loved and encouraged all branches of agriculture. Some of these "were in the desert," that is, in the district to the southeast of Jerusalem, on the west of the Dead Sea, an extensive grazing district "in the low country" lying between the mountains of Judah and the Mediterranean; "and in the plains," east of the Jordan, within the territory of Reuben (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.43">De 4:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.20.8">Jos 20:8</reference>).<div eID="gen5955" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5956" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in Carmel--</hi>This mountain, being within the boundary of Israel, did not belong to Uzziah; and as it is here placed in opposition to the vine-bearing mountains, it is probably used, not as a proper name, but to signify, as the word denotes, "fruitful fields" (Margin).<div eID="gen5956" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5957" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2Chr.26.11-2Chr.26.15">2Ch 26:11-15</reference>. His Host, and Engines of War. <div eID="gen5957" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
10. Also he built towers in the desert-- for the threefold purpose of defense, of observation, and of shelter to his cattle. He dug also a great many wells, for he loved and encouraged all branches of agriculture. Some of these "were in the desert," that is, in the district to the southeast of Jerusalem, on the west of the Dead Sea, an extensive grazing district "in the low country" lying between the mountains of Judah and the Mediterranean; "and in the plains," east of the Jordan, within the territory of Reuben ( De 4:43 ; Jos 20:8 ).

 in Carmel-- This mountain, being within the boundary of Israel, did not belong to Uzziah; and as it is here placed in opposition to the vine-bearing mountains, it is probably used, not as a proper name, but to signify, as the word denotes, "fruitful fields" (Margin).

 2Ch 26:11-15 . His Host, and Engines of War.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4111"/><div sID="gen5958" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4111"/><hi type="bold">11-15. an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands--</hi>He raised a strong body of militia, divided into companies or regiments of uniform size, which served in rotation. The enumeration was performed by two functionaries expert in the drawing up of military muster-rolls, under the superintendence of Hananiah, one of the high officers of the crown. The army consisted of 307,500 picked men, under the command of two thousand gallant officers, chiefs or heads of fathers' houses, so that each father's house formed a distinct band. They were fully equipped with every kind of military accoutrements, from brazen helmets, a habergeon or coat of mail, to a sling for stones. <div eID="gen5958" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4113"/><div sID="gen5962" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4113"/><hi type="bold">16-21. he transgressed against the Lord, &c.--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="2Kgs.15.5">2Ki 15:5</reference>). This daring and wicked act is in both records traced to the intoxicating influence of overweening pride and vanity. But here the additional circumstances are stated, that his entrance was opposed, and strong remonstrances made (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.10">1Ch 6:10</reference>) by the high priest, who was accompanied by eighty inferior priests. Rage and threats were the only answers he deigned to return, but God took care to vindicate the sacredness of the priestly office. At the moment the king lifted the censer, He struck him with leprosy. The earthquake mentioned (<reference osisRef="Amos.1.1">Am 1:1</reference>) is said to have been felt at the moment [Josephus]. <div eID="gen5962" type="x-p"/>
